A 56-year-old postmenopausal woman presents to the clinic with several weeks of vague abdominal
discomfort. She denies symptoms such as dysuria, flank pain, constipation, or vaginal bleeding. Her
medical history is notable for well-controlled hypertension managed with lisinopril, and her surgical
history includes two cesarean sections. On examination, her temperature is 98.6 ºF, blood pressure is
114/83 mmHg, pulse is 84/min, and respiratory rate is 20/min. Auscultation reveals diminished breath
sounds over the right lower lung fields without wheezes or rhonchi. Abdominal examination shows
diffuse tenderness and a positive fluid wave. Bimanual pelvic examination identifies right adnexal
fullness. Which histopathologic finding in the ovary is most consistent with this clinical presentation?
Answer Choices: (A) Irregularly narrowed tubules with papillary branching (B) Granulosa cells arranged
in a Call-Exner body pattern (C) Uniformly small, round cells with scant cytoplasm (D) Mucin-filled
glandular structures (E) Spindle-shaped fibroblast bundle (F) Sheets of large, pleomorphic cells with
necrosis (G) Signet-ring cells within glandular tissue (H) Thecal cell hyperplasia (I) Psammoma bodies
surrounded by serous epithelium (J) Lipid-laden stromal cells
 A. Granulosa cells arranged in a Call-Exner body pattern
B. Lipid-laden stromal cells
C. Irregularly narrowed tubules with papillary branching
D. Sheets of large, pleomorphic cells with necrosis
E. Spindle-shaped fibroblast bundle
F. Mucin-filled glandular structures
G. Psammoma bodies surrounded by serous epithelium
H. Signet-ring cells within glandular tissue
I. Uniformly small, round cells with scant cytoplasm
J. Thecal cell hyperplasia
